title: SLO-driven telemetry orchestration for enterprise cutover
author: Aisha Benitez
content:
Overview
--------
This playbook defines the SLO-driven telemetry and automated-orchestration patterns used during enterprise cutovers (provisioned Dedicated or Private tenants) and the post-cutover stabilization window. It is intended for Customer Success (CS), Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), and the onboarding customer engineering teams. The goal is to detect regressions quickly, drive automated mitigations where safe, and provide clean inputs into QBRs and post-incident reviews.

Scope
-----
- Applies to: Dedicated tenants, Private deployments (VPC/on-prem), and any high-commit enterprise account cutover.
- Excludes: Small self-serve accounts and non-production sandbox cutovers.
- Timebox: Primary playbook focuses on the first 72 hours after cutover (Day 0 -> Day 3).

Goals and Acceptance Criteria
-----------------------------
- Detect customer-impacting regressions within 5 minutes of onset for critical SLOs (latency, availability, error rate).
- Automatically reduce non-critical throughput (traffic shaping) within 10 minutes when token cost or latency SLOs are violated.
- Maintain p95 inference latency <= 250 ms for low-latency tiers; error rate < 0.5% (HTTP 5xx & model errors) during cutover.
- Produce a QBR-ready cutover report (SLO timeline + remediation actions) within 48 hours of cutover completion.

Roles and Responsibilities
--------------------------
- Customer Success (owner): coordinate cutover cadence, communications, stakeholder alignment, runbook execution.
- SRE (owner): author and own alerts, automation playbooks, capacity throttles, and rollback primitives.
- Solutions/Onboarding Engineer: performs tenant-specific validations, smoke tests, and acceptance gating.
- Customer Engineering (customer): participates in acceptance tests and approves go/no-go.

Key SLOs and Signals to Monitor
-------------------------------
- Availability SLO: requests with 2xx/3xx >= 99.95% over rolling 1h. Alert: drop below 99.9% for 10m.
- Latency SLOs: p50/p95/p99 for token generation RPCs. Example targets: p50 <= 70ms, p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 600ms. Alert: p95 > 350ms for 5m.
- Error Rate: API-level 5xx + model-internal errors <= 0.5% over 15m. Alert: >= 1% sustained for 5m.
- Cost per 1k tokens (telemetry): track to detect runaway unit-costs; alert when > 2x expected baseline for 30m.
- KV/Cache Hit Ratio: goal >= 85% for workloads using prefix caching. Alert: drop below 70%.
- Queueing Depth / Backpressure: queue length per instance > 100 for 3m -> trigger autoscaler or shed traffic.

Instrumentation and Data Sources
--------------------------------
- Metrics: Prometheus-style metrics for request_latency_ms (histogram), request_success_total, request_failure_total, token_cost_total, kv_cache_hit_total.
- Traces: Distributed traces forwarded to the central tracing cluster (Jaeger/Tempo). Ensure 1:100 sampling at minimum during cutover window.
- Logs: Structured JSON request logs (request_id, tenant_id, model_id, seq_len, latency_ms, error_code). Indexed and searchable for at least 7 days.
- Telemetry Gateway: tenant-specific forwarder that tags data with tenant_id and cutover_phase.

Example Prometheus alert rules (copy into SRE alerting repo)
------------------------------------------------------------
- name: CutoverSLOs
  rules:
  - alert: TenantHighLatencyCutover
    expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_latency_ms_bucket{tenant_id=~"TENANT_REPLACE"}[5m])) by (le)) > 350
    for: 5m
    labels:
      severity: page
    annotations:
      summary: "p95 latency > 350ms for {{ $labels.tenant_id }}"

  - alert: TenantAvailabilityDrop
    expr: (sum(rate(request_success_total{tenant_id=~"TENANT_REPLACE"}[10m])) / sum(rate(request_success_total{tenant_id=~"TENANT_REPLACE"}[10m]) + rate(request_failure_total{tenant_id=~"TENANT_REPLACE"}[10m]))) < 0.999
    for: 10m
    labels:
      severity: page
    annotations:
      summary: "Availability below 99.9% for {{ $labels.tenant_id }}"

Automated Orchestration Patterns
--------------------------------
We support three levels of automated actions. All automation must be gated by safe-guards and require an owner to sign-off for rollbacks.
1) Non-blocking mitigation (automated, no human approval)
   - Examples: switch on aggressive batching for affected model variant, increase KV cache TTL, temporary token-rate shaping for non-critical routes.
   - Trigger conditions: p95 latency breach for 5 minutes AND queue_depth > threshold.
   - Safety checks: only allowed for tenants with 'auto-mitigate' flag enabled; actions are reversible and logged.

2) Assisted remediation (automated runbook + human confirm)
   - Examples: scale dedicated GPU pool by adding burst nodes, switch to lower-cost quantized model variant and notify CS + SRE.
   - Trigger conditions: cost per 1k tokens > 2x baseline OR error rate spike > 1%.
   - Human step: on-call SRE must acknowledge within 15 minutes or system reverts to conservative traffic shaping.

3) Rollback (manual, highest impact)
   - Examples: rollback to previous model version, failover to hosted pool, or revert tenant network configuration.
   - Preconditions: requires product owner + CS + SRE approval.
   - Trigger conditions: sustained violation of Availability SLO for 30m or safety checks indicating data corruption.

Runbook: Pre-Cutover Checklist (Day -7 to Day 0)
------------------------------------------------
1) Confirm business stakeholders and cutover window.
2) Verify SRE alerting templates cloned and tenant_id variables configured.
3) Validate telemetry forwarding for tenant (Prometheus relabels, trace sampling, log pipeline).
4) Smoke test with synthetic traffic: 10k tokens/min for 30 minutes; confirm p95 latency and success-rate.
5) Baseline cost measurement: record expected token cost and model selection.
6) Confirm automated-mitigation flags with customer.
7) Preload KV cache with canonical prefixes where applicable.

Runbook: Day 0 (Cutover) Steps
------------------------------
1) Coordinate go/no-go with customer and CS lead.
2) Start cutover marker: set cutover_phase=active on telemetry gateway.
3) Run smoke tests for each critical route (synchronous generation, streaming, embeddings) and confirm success.
4) Observe SLO dashboards for first 30m with 1m refresh cadence.
5) If p95 > 350ms or availability < 99.9%, trigger Non-blocking Mitigation sequence (see automation).
6) If mitigations do not normalize SLOs in 15m, escalate to Assisted remediation.

Runbook: Day 1-3 (Post-cutover Stabilization)
-------------------------------------------
- Maintain elevated sampling and dashboard refresh intervals.
- Run periodic synthetic tests every 2 hours.
- Capture representative traces and attach to cutover incident.
- Produce interim cutover report at 24h with the following sections: traffic profile, SLO timeline, interventions applied, customer impact estimate, and recommended next steps.

Escalation Matrix and Contacts
-----------------------------
- Page (P0): SRE on-call (pager duty) -> primary on-call + backup.
- CS escalation: CS lead (Aisha Benitez) -> solutions engineer -> account executive (if customer-visible outage).
- Product / Model owner: for model-behavior regressions.
- Security: security-oncall for data-exposure concerns.
Contact formatting example: role: name (channel) / pager.

Rollback Criteria and Safe-Rollback Procedure
--------------------------------------------
Rollback is a last-resort action. Criteria for rollback include:
- Availability < 99% for 30m and no recoverable cause found.
- Data integrity concerns (new model producing unsafe labels or PII leakage).
- Unacceptable cost surge causing billing exposure >= 3x baseline.

Safe-rollback steps (high-level):
1) Freeze auto-mitigation changes and document current state.
2) Notify stakeholders and schedule immediate rollback conference.
3) Execute rollback in maintenance window: revert model version or failover to hosted pool.
4) Validate smoke tests (same as pre-cutover).
5) Re-open cutover review and plan root-cause analysis.

QBR integration: Cutover Report Template (deliver within 48h)
---------------------------------------------------------
- Executive summary (1 paragraph): success state and any customer-visible impact.
- Key metrics: Availability, p95 latency, error rate, cost per 1k tokens, KV cache hit ratio.
- Timeline: annotated SLO graph (timestamps of mitigations & escalations).
- Actions taken: automated and manual.
- Open items & follow-ups: model tuning, capacity commitment, telemetry gaps.

Testing and Validation Guidance
------------------------------
- Synthetic traffic generator (recommended CLI):
  rcli cutover-test --tenant TENANT_REPLACE --duration 30m --tokens-per-sec 167 --routes "generation,streaming,embedding"
- Acceptance criteria for tests: all core routes meet p95 targets and success-rate >= 99.9%.
- Include chaos testing (network latency injection) during staging cutover to validate failover logic.

Auditability and Post-Incident Attachment Requirements
----------------------------------------------------
- All automated actions must write a reversible change record to the cutover incident log with: timestamp, actor, action-id, and revert procedure.
- Attach 3 representative traces for every automated mitigation and 10 for every rollback.
- Retain cutover incident artifacts for 90 days.

Maintenance and Runbook Ownership
--------------------------------
- This document is owned by Customer Success. SRE maintains the alerting rules and automation repository.
- Review cadence: every cutover OR quarterly, whichever is sooner.
- Change process: propose change in the CS runbook PR board; SRE must approve changes to alerts/automation.

References and Links
-------------------
- SRE alerting repo: git+ssh://git.internal.redwood/sre/alerts (replace TENANT_REPLACE variables as required).
- Cutover incident template: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortems/cutover-incident-template
- QBR dashboard template: /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/qbr-cutover-template

Appendix: Example Grafana Panel queries
-------------------------------------
- p95 latency (PromQL): histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_latency_ms_bucket{tenant_id=~"TENANT_REPLACE"}[5m])) by (le))
- Availability ratio: sum(rate(request_success_total{tenant_id=~"TENANT_REPLACE"}[5m])) / (sum(rate(request_success_total{tenant_id=~"TENANT_REPLACE"}[5m])) + sum(rate(request_failure_total{tenant_id=~"TENANT_REPLACE"}[5m])))

End of document.
